findings.title: Faith as a response that takes time
findings.claim: The earlier sequence depicts faith as assent that responds to signs and reminders through bodily worship and purposive, reparative action; this makes the focus's question of benefit concern whether assent still has time to become a lived response.
findings.mechanism: The same assent branch appears in the focus and in 32:15, where signs and reminders are followed by falling in prostration and praise; 32:19 pairs faith with action and righteous work. These wider acts meet the focus's assent and benefit carriers, shifting faith from a detachable credential to a trajectory that takes time to appear in conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees what practical benefit can mean: a response with bodily and reparative consequences, not merely a profession stated at the endpoint.
findings.containment: The earlier verses show how responsive faith is portrayed but do not prove that action is the causal means of benefit; the deeds may instead be evidence of genuine faith. HFT context word indices and unresolved roots remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: Exact context Arabic and HFT coordinates are present, but most context root/branch identities are unresolved and remain attributed.

branch_activations.activation: The earlier assent construction is embodied in acts, and the focus's benefit clause then asks whether late assent can still take that path.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Faith can be read as a response trajectory whose effects need time, not only a belief-state named at the endpoint.

findings.title: A compressed reply under scarcity
findings.claim: The focus imperative remains an ordinary command, while its packet-mapped non-dominant scarcity target meets the earlier phrase of little gratitude; joined to the denied extension, the reply feels compressed into one decisive fact when usable time is scarce.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace maps a scarcity branch to the focus command's sound/root target and independently cites 32:9's explicit low-gratitude expression on the same mapped target. The focus's separate no-respite word then supplies a scarcity of remaining interval. The contact makes the answer feel narrowed by little prior response and little remaining time without turning the imperative into a scarcity word morphologically.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the reply's compression as part of its timing: the answer comes when the interval for a different response has nearly disappeared.
findings.containment: This is the packet-sanctioned split-root sound-and-root resonance, not a morphological reanalysis of qul and not a translation of the imperative as fewness. The mapping and context index are legacy-unbound, so the reading remains exploratory.

epistemic.reason: The HFT outlier supplies exact focus/context Arabic and a split-root trace, but the target is explicitly non-dominant and morphology does not make the command mean scarcity.

The HFT summary also leaves the main cause of late faith's non-benefit unresolved among compelled recognition, expired action-time, and prior status. The retained readings keep these alternatives compatible rather than deciding among them.
